_comment: Motion tokens. `docs/design-tokens.md` §6 and `docs/accessibility.md` §3.6 have listed Motion/Duration/* and Motion/Easing/* as required token categories since before this file existed, but no source file implemented them — this file closes that gap. Added 2026-07-28 during the ContentState sync (Figma node 1174:1355), whose Loading variant is the first shipped component with real, Figma-authored keyframe data. Sourcing: `duration.slow` (2000ms) and the `skeleton-pulse` group are exact, read from that node's animation via get_motion_context — a 2s looping opacity track on every skeleton bar, easing easeInOut between the dimmed and full stops, with each bar's dip offset along the timeline to produce a staggered wave. The remaining duration steps and every easing curve have NO Figma source: Figma publishes no motion variable collection, so they are conventional Material-style values recorded here as PROVISIONAL, and exist so components stop reaching for raw ms/cubic-bezier literals. Do not treat them as design-approved; reconcile them if a motion collection is ever published. Every consumer must pair these with a prefers-reduced-motion branch per docs/accessibility.md §3.6 — the tokens carry no reduced-motion behavior of their own.

fast.usage: Hover, focus, and other immediate affordance feedback. Provisional.

moderate.usage: Enter/exit of small surfaces — popovers, tooltips, toasts. Provisional.

slow.usage: Larger surfaces — drawers, modals, panel resize. Provisional.

skeleton-pulse.usage: One full loop of the ContentState loading skeleton's opacity wave.
skeleton-pulse._comment: Exact, from Figma node 1174:1355's timeline cohort (durationMs 2000, loopMode 'loop').

toast.usage: Toast auto-dismiss delay and progress-bar countdown.
toast._comment: Direct user request ('show the toaster message for 6 seconds and automatically closed after 6 seconds'), not Figma-sourced — get_motion_context on node 1475:5100 returns no keyframe data; the Toast frame is a static mockup with 3 snapshot instances at different progress-bar fill widths illustrating the concept, not an animated prototype.

hero-rotate.usage: EnterpriseLoginPage hero illustration's ambient background spin — one full 0deg->360deg clockwise rotation, linear timing.
hero-rotate._comment: Direct user request ('subtle rotating animation... expert level recommendation', approved with 'figma doesn't have the animation background, please go ahead'), then corrected same day per explicit follow-up ('rotate the dotted SVG smoothly clockwise... I don't see the smooth rotation') from an initial small oscillating -3deg/+3deg wobble to this full continuous spin — the wobble had been chosen to avoid sweeping gaps past the image's own bounding box (a landscape ~824x580 dot cloud bled across a portrait panel), but that risk doesn't actually apply here: the panel's own background (`--color-primary-900`) already matches the illustration's transparent negative space, and the static (pre-animation) crop already leaves areas of the panel uncovered by the image with no visible seam — a full rotation sweeps that same already-invisible boundary around instead of introducing a new one. Linear (not eased) timing is deliberate: an eased continuous loop visibly speeds up/slows down at the seam, which reads as a stutter, not "smooth".

hero-glimmer.usage: EnterpriseLoginPage hero illustration's sparkle-dot twinkle — one full fade-in/fade-out cycle per dot.
hero-glimmer._comment: Same request/approval as hero-rotate, same no-Figma-source caveat. Reuses the existing `stagger.skeleton-step-*` fractions (already generic 0/0.075/0.15/0.225/0.3-of-loop offsets, not skeleton-specific in shape) to stagger 5 sparkle dots rather than defining a new stagger set.

standard.usage: Default for state changes. Provisional — no Figma source.

enter.usage: Elements entering the viewport. Provisional — no Figma source.

exit.usage: Elements leaving the viewport. Provisional — no Figma source.

emphasized.usage: Large or attention-carrying transitions. Provisional — no Figma source.

skeleton-pulse.usage: Segment easing between the ContentState skeleton's full and dimmed opacity stops.
skeleton-pulse._comment: Exact, from Figma node 1174:1355 — get_motion_context reports easeInOut on the dip segments and linear on the hold segments; the holds are expressed as keyframe percentages in the generated @keyframes rather than as a separate easing token.

skeleton-pulse-from.usage: ContentState skeleton bar opacity at rest and at the end of each loop.

skeleton-pulse-to.usage: ContentState skeleton bar opacity at the dimmest point of the wave.
skeleton-pulse-to._comment: Exact, from Figma node 1174:1355. Note this is 0.4, NOT the 0.5 that Tailwind's core `animate-pulse` uses — the shared Skeleton primitive keeps animate-pulse; ContentState's skeleton bars use this Figma-exact value instead.

stagger._comment: Exact, from Figma node 1174:1355. get_motion_context returns each skeleton bar as its own opacity track with the same waveform (hold at full -> dip to 0.4 across 30% of the loop -> return to full across the next 30% -> hold), differing only in where along the 2s timeline the dip begins: 0, 0.075, 0.15, 0.225 and 0.3 of the loop. That is one shared @keyframes plus a per-bar animation-delay, not five different animations — so it is recorded as a fraction of the loop here and multiplied by duration.skeleton-pulse at emit time. The build emits these as ms in --duration-skeleton-stagger-*.

skeleton-step-1.usage: Skeleton subtitle, and table-row first cell.

skeleton-step-2.usage: Card label, and table-row second cell.

skeleton-step-3.usage: Card value, and table-row third cell.

skeleton-step-4.usage: Card meta, and table-row fourth cell.
